## Global Colors

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/global-colors/>

ColorMag includes a powerful Global Color System that gives you full control over your site’s look and feel from a single place.

Using color palettes, custom palettes, global linking, and dark mode support, you can change your entire website’s color scheme instantly—without editing individual elements.

This article explains how the system works and how to use it effectively.

You can find Global color settings under: **Appearance → Customize → Global → Colors **

## **Color Palette**

The Color Palette controls the overall color theme of your website.

ColorMag provides several predefined palettes, each containing 9 colors designed to work harmoniously across your layout.

When you select or change a palette, any element that uses Global Colors will automatically update to match the global preset.

### **Palette Color Purpose**

Each palette includes the following colors:

**Color NameColor CategoryColor PurposeMain AccentAccent Colors ** Primary brand color used for buttons, links, call-to-action, and main highlights.
**Secondary AccentAccent Colors ** Supporting accent for hover states, tags, badges, and subtle highlights
**Main BackgroundBackground Colors ** Default background for general page areas
**Surface BackgroundBackground Colors** Background for cards, panels, and elevated sections
**Contrast BackgroundBackground Colors ** Background for headers, footers, hero sections, or areas requiring high visual contrast
**Title TextText Colors** Color used for headings text
**Regular TextText Colors ** Color for body text, paragraphs, content text
**Text on ContrastText Colors ** Text color displayed on dark/contrast backgrounds
**MutedUtility Color ** Subtle color for lines, dividers, outlines, captions, and secondary text

**Viewing Color Names**

When you hover over or click any color in the palette, its name appears, helping you understand its purpose.

**Note**: All new ColorMag demos are designed using these preset palettes. You can instantly transform the demo’s appearance by selecting a different palette.

## **Creating a Custom Palette**

You can create your own palette to match your brand colors.

**To add a custom palette:**

- Go to Global Colors (Appearance → Customize → Global → Colors)

- Click Add Custom Palette

- Enter a name

- Select a base palette from the Extend Palette dropdown

- Click Add to create your palette

- Click any color to edit it using the color picker

You can delete custom palettes from the same interface.

## **Customizing Color Palette**

You can customize both the predefined palettes and your custom palettes.

**Edit Colors** – Click on any area of the color palette to open it. Then, select any color in the palette to access the picker, where you can choose your preferred shade.

**Delete Palette** – Click the delete icon beside a custom palette to remove it. You cannot delete predefined palettes.

**Saving Changes** – When you select or edit a palette, the changes apply instantly. Click Publish to save them permanently.

## **Theme Colors**

Below the palette section, you’ll find the Theme Colors panel, which defines the default colors for the major areas of your website. These settings act as global defaults that can be overridden for specific elements elsewhere in the Customizer.

- **Primary Color** – Accent color used to highlight important elements across your site. Defaults to “Main Accent” from the active color palette.

- **Base** – Global default color for all text elements. Defaults to “Regular Text” from the active color palette.

- **Links** – Default colors for links throughout your site:

- **First color circle:** Normal link color (defaults to “Main Accent”)

- **Second color circle:** Hover link color (defaults to “Secondary Accent”)

- **Headings** – Global default color for all heading text (h1-h6). Defaults to “Title Text” from the active color palette. You can set different colors for different heading tags (h1-h6) from Typography settings.

- **Container Inside BackgroundPro** – The background for the content area inside your container. You can add either a solid color or background image.

- **Container Outside BackgroundPro** – The background for the area outside your container. You can add either a solid color or background image. **Note:** This option only works if you have selected a Boxed Layout for your container width.

## **Dark Skin (Dark Mode) **Pro

If you use the Color Switcher widget in the Header/Footer Builder, the Dark Skin settings define the colors used in dark mode.

When visitors toggle the color switcher, the palette chosen under Skin Color becomes the second color scheme.

Important: Even if individual elements use custom (non-global) colors, Dark Skin overrides them for a complete dark mode experience.

## **Global Colors in Customizer**

To assign a global color to any element in the Customizer:

- Click the color icon in the element to open the color picker

- View the active palette colors shown in the top row

- Hover over a color circle to see its name

- Select the global color you want

When you choose a predefined color from the active palette, a small 🌐 globe icon appears in the top-left corner of the color indicator.

**Important:** If you manually choose a custom color (not from the palette), it will not be updated when you change palettes.

## **Global Colors in Gutenberg / Block Editor**

ColorMag global colors can be used across Gutenberg blocks. When you update or change the palette from the Customizer, all blocks using Global Colors update automatically—no need to edit blocks individually.

**To use Global Colors in the Block Editor:**

- Select any block

- Go to the Color settings

- Choose a color from the Theme section

All palette colors appear automatically in the block editor’s color picker.

## **Global Colors in Elementor**

ColorMag Global Colors integrate seamlessly with Elementor. When you update or change your palette in the Customizer, Elementor styles using Global Colors update automatically.

**To use Global Colors in Elementor:**

- Open an Elementor element’s color settings

- Click the 🌐 globe icon

- You’ll see:

- Elementor’s global colors

- ColorMag Global Colors (prefixed with ColorMag)

- Select any “ColorMag” global color

**Note:** ColorMag’s global colors are labeled with ColorMag for easy identification.

## Global Typography

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/global-typography/>

ColorMag includes a powerful Global Typography system that lets you control font family, sizes, and text styling from a single place.

With typography presets, options for body text, headings, individual heading tags, responsive controls, and dedicated typography control options, you can create a clean, readable, and visually consistent design across all pages.

This article explains how the typography system works and how to use it effectively.

You can access Typography settings under: **Appearance → Customize → Global → Typography**

## **Presets**

Typography Presets allow you to instantly apply a complete font pairing across your whole website. ColorMag includes 6 professionally designed presets.

Presets control the overall typography across your entire site. Clicking a preset automatically updates both the body font and heading font.

- Each preset includes one **Heading font** and one **Body font**.

- When you hover over a preset, you’ll see the font pair displayed in the format:
**Heading Font / Body Font** (e.g., Outfit / DM Sans ).

- Clicking a preset automatically updates global heading and body fonts.

You can reset to the default font pair (Open Sans / Open Sans for both heading and body text) by clicking the reset icon beside the **Presets** label.

## **Typography control options**

To edit typography settings, click the typography summary button (e.g., ‘Lato / 14px / 400’). This label shows the currently applied font family, size, and weight.
This opens the full typography panel where you can adjust all styling options.

**Available SettingsSettingPurposeFont Family** Choose from many Google Fonts.
**Font Weight** Controls thickness (300, 400, 500, 700). Available weights depend on the selected font.
**Font Size** Set font size with responsive controls (Desktop, Tablet, Mobile)
**Line Height** Controls vertical spacing between text lines. Recommended values: Body 1.4–1.8, Headings 1.1–1.3.
**Letter Spacing** Adjust spacing between characters
**Font Style** Normal or Italic
**Text Transform** None, Uppercase, Lowercase, or Capitalize.

You can preview changes live before saving. Changes only become permanent when you click **Publish**.

## **Body**

Body Typography controls the main reading text across your website — including posts, pages, sidebar text, and footer content.

You can adjust font family, weight, font size, line height, letter spacing, style, and text transform.

**Notes:**

- These settings apply site-wide unless a specific section overrides them.

- For best readability on mobile, use separate font sizes via the device icons.

## **Heading**

Heading Typography sets the global font styling for all headings (**H1–H6**) at once.

This helps you maintain consistent typography hierarchy across your site.

## **Individual Heading Levels (H1–H6)**

You can customize each heading tag (H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, H6) separately for more fine-tuned control.

By default, each heading level inherits the Global Heading Font Family, which is recommended for performance.

However, you can individually customize Font size (responsive), Font weight, Line height, Letter spacing, Text transform as needed.

This allows full control of typography hierarchy, for example, making H1 significantly larger and bolder while setting moderate sizes for H2 and H3.

Note: If you adjust the typography of a specific heading, it will override the global heading settings.

### **Individual Heading ColorsPro**

You can also set a custom color for each heading level.
By default, all heading tags inherit the Global Heading Color , but you can override this at any time.

To change a heading color, click the color icon next to the typography control and choose either a custom color or a color from the active global palette.

This allows you to give different heading levels their own color styling whenever needed.

## **Responsive Typography Controls**

ColorMag gives device-based control for:

- Font size

- Line height

- Letter spacing

You can switch between:

- **Desktop**

- **Tablet**

- **Mobile**

by clicking the device icons next to each setting.

This ensures your text remains clear, readable, and well-scaled on all screen sizes.

## **Typography in Gutenberg / Block Editor**

Global Typography applies automatically to most Gutenberg blocks that use default theme styles, including:

- Paragraphs

- Headings

- Lists

- Buttons

- Columns

- Group blocks

- Site Title & Tagline

To keep everything consistent, leave the font family as Default and keep other settings unchanged. You can override global typography by setting typography at the block level.

## **Typography in Elementor**

ColorMag’s Global Typography works inside Elementor as long as the widget’s font setting is left as Default. If you manually pick a font or change typography inside Elementor, those settings will override the Customizer typography.

#### Disable Default Fonts in Elementor

To make Elementor inherit all typography from ColorMag:

- Go to **WordPress Admin → Elementor → Settings → General**

- Enable the option: **Disable Default Fonts.**

This tells Elementor to stop using its own built-in font system and instead use the typography defined in your theme.

When Elementor’s default fonts are disabled, all Elementor widgets automatically inherit ColorMag’s Global Typography, including headings and body text. You don’t need to configure typography separately inside Elementor.

## Customize the Button

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/customize-the-button/>

**Location**: Appearance → Customize → Global→ Button

A Button in a site refers to a clickable option helping the user navigate to other sections or pages. ColorMag supports adding the button and allows customizing with various options listed below:

## Button

The section customizes the Button added on the site with the following options:

### **Color **

It changes the **Color** of the text added inside the button.

Change Button Text Color

### **Background**

It changes the **Background** color of the button.

Change Button Background Color

### **Typography **Pro

It controls the button text** Typography**, such as **Font Family**, **Weight**, **Font size**,** Line height**, and other related styling properties for the text.

Change Button Typography

## Padding

It sets the button padding spaces for all four sides, i.e., Left, Right, Top, and Bottom.

Change Button Padding

## Border **Pro**

It customizes the Border area that appears around the button and comes with the following options:

### **Style**

It allows you to choose the border **Style** to be None, Solid, Double, Dashed, or Dotted

Change Button Border Style

### **Width **

It determines the **size** of the border.

Change Button Border Width

### **Color **Pro

It allows you to change the **Color** of the border.

Change Button Border Color

### **Radius**

It sets the **Curve** of the border on the corners of the box. You can move the slider to the right area to increase the radius value.

## Manage Sidebar Area Layout

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/manage-sidebar-area-layout/>

**Location:** Appearance → Customize → Global → Sidebar → Layout

The Sidebar is the vertical column representing additional information, navigations, ads, etc., displayed on the website page’s left or right side. You can either place the Sidebar on the left, right, or both or not display it.

ColorMag allows changing the Sidebar layout on various pages. It means you can place the Sidebar on different areas for different pages. For example – You can set the **Blog** page to have a **Left Sidebar**, the **Single Post** page to have a **Right Sidebar**, and so on.

Currenlty, there are three layout areas where the sidebar changes will be reflected listed below:

- **Default Layout **– The changes apply to all the pages/posts of the site.

- **Blog/ Archive** – The changes apply to all the Blog/Archive of the site.

- **Page** – The changes apply to all the pages created on the site.

- **Single Post** – The changes apply to the single post pages only.

With the ColorMag theme, there are five available sidebar options to be chosen, which are listed below:

## Left Sidebar

It sets the Sidebar on the left of the main content. It can be added via **Appearance → Customize → Widgets → Left Sidebar**.

Content with Left Sidebar

## Right Sidebar

It sets the Sidebar on the right of the main content. It can be added via **Appearance → Customize → Widgets → Right Sidebar**.

Content with Right Sidebar

## Full-Width Sidebar

It hides the Sidebar and sets the main content to be displayed on the entire screen.

Content with Full-width Layout

## Center Content

It hides the Sidebar and sets the main content to be displayed in the center.

Content with Center Layout

## Two Sidebar

It displays the Sidebar in both areas, i.e., Left and Right. It can be added via **Appearance → Customize → Widgets → Left and Right Sidebar**.

Content with Left and Right Sidebars

A sticky sidebar refers to a design where the sidebar is fixed in its position while scrolling the site below. It helps to access the important information on the sidebar even while scrolling down.

## Widget Title **Pro**

It refers to the title of the widgets that are added to the sidebar. With this section, you can customize the widget title with the following options:

## Manage Container Area Layout and Width

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/manage-container-area-layout-and-width/>

**Location:** Appearance → Customize → Global → Layout

**Layout** refers to the area or space where the main content of the website is placed. Basically, it is an area where we display the content. ColorMag allows customizing the container area with various options listed below.

## Global Layout

Within the Customizer > Global > Layout, you will find the global layout option, this will affect every content within your website and ensure they follow the layout style you have set. This can be overridden by individual post type settings, which we will get to in a bit.

### Layout options:

- **Normal**– In this layout, the content follows a strict width of 1140px. This is the normal setting.

- **Narrow** – In this layout, the content follows a strict width of 800px.

If you would like to add your own custom width, that is only available in the PRO version, where you can input your own width. Checkout ColorMag PRO here

### Layout style:

- Boxed style – A box surrounds your content area, your header and footer will not extend past a certain width and they will be ‘boxed’

- Wide – While your content spans as per the layout setting, your header and footer will continue to span the full screen width.

### Sidebar layout

You may also globally select a sidebar layout to show throughout the website. You can select:

- Hide the sidebar altogether.

- Show to the right.

- Show to the left.

While the setting within Global applies to all pages, it can be overridden too. This can be useful if you don’t want to show sidebar or would like to have a separate layout width on single blog pages. For that you will have to navigate to:

Appearance → Customize → Post Types → {Post type name}

From here you can select post types like:

- Blog – Archive pages, that show a collection of posts

- Single post – When a user interacts with a single post, this template is applied.

- Page – When a user views a page, this template is applied.

Each of these can have a different layout style to give a variable experience to your users. Upon clicking on any of these:

You will find:

- Layout option – Same as before, when set to inherit, this will follow the same setting within Global > Layout. To override, you may change it to whatever you desire.

- Sidebar – Just like before, inherit follows the global setting, to override, select one from the listed.

Just like before, for custom width values and more customizability, you will have to get ColorMag PRO. Check it out here

- **Post elements** – This is the order in which elements will show up, you may drag and drop them where you desire and also customize other settings for the elements too.

- **Post meta** – Same as the post elements, this one is for the meta items like Date, Author, views and so on.

- **Related posts toggle** – If you would like to show related posts before the end of the content, you may enable this and it will show related posts of the category in that page template.
